strawberry_healthy.description: Foliage exhibits vibrant green coloration, uniform leaf turgor, intact margins, and no visible lesions, chlorosis, or necrotic spotting.
symptoms: Deep uniform green trifoliate leaves with serrated margins
Vigorous crown growth with upright petioles
Absence of fungal spots, powdery mildew, or marginal necrosis
causes: Adequate soil drainage and clean weed-free bed management

organic: Continue maintenance sprays of diluted neem oil (0.5%) as a prophylactic repellent
Apply beneficial compost tea to sustain healthy phyllosphere microflora
chemical: No chemical fungicides or bactericides required for healthy foliage

fertilizer: Maintain balanced N-P-K (such as 10-10-10 or 12-12-12) during vegetative establishment
Shift to higher potassium and calcium (e.g., 5-10-15 with chelated calcium) during flower bud initiation and fruit sizing
Avoid excess nitrogen which results in soft foliage vulnerable to fungal spore penetration
irrigation: Deliver 1.0 - 1.5 inches of water per week using drip tape placed beneath plastic mulch
Strictly avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation to keep the canopy dry
Water early in the morning to allow any surface moisture to evaporate before midday
prevention: Utilize certified disease-free bare-root or plug transplants from reputable nurseries
Maintain raised beds covered with straw or UV-stabilized plastic mulch to elevate foliage from wet soil
Ensure minimum 12-inch spacing between plants in staggered rows for laminar air circulation
recovery_tips: Remove senescent or damaged runner leaves during routine weekly scouting
Maintain clean field borders to prevent weed-harbored insect vectors

strawberry_leaf_scorch.description: Leaf scorch produces numerous small, irregular purple or dark reddish-brown blotches on the upper surface of leaves. As lesions coalesce, the entire leaf turns brown, curls upward at the margins, and takes on a scorched appearance.
symptoms: Small, angular, purplish to dark-brown spots without white centers on upper leaf surfaces
Spots coalesce causing extensive blotching, leaf curling, and burnt brown margins
Lesions can also appear on petiole stems, calyxes, and fruit caps, turning them brown and brittle
causes: Prolonged leaf wetness (6 to 9 hours of continuous moisture at 15-25°C)
Overhead sprinkler irrigation that splashes fungal conidia across adjacent crowns
Dense canopy with poor air movement and high relative humidity

severity_rules.mild: < 10% coverage; isolated purple flecks restricted to older lower leaves
severity_rules.moderate: 10% - 30% coverage; coalesced necrotic patches with partial leaf curling
severity_rules.severe: > 30% coverage; widespread canopy scorch, dry necrotic margins, and calyx infection

organic: Spray copper hydroxide or copper octanoate (bordeaux mixture) at early symptom emergence
Apply bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or Trichoderma harzianum at 7-day intervals
Prune and safely bag heavily scorched leaves to reduce primary inoculum load
chemical: Apply protectant fungicides such as Captan 50WP (2.5 lb/acre) or Thiram
For active outbreaks, apply systemic FRAC group 3 or group 11 fungicides (e.g., Pyraclostrobin, Azoxystrobin, or Difenoconazole)
Rotate fungicide FRAC chemical groups every 14 days to mitigate pathogen resistance development

fertilizer: Halt high-nitrogen fertilizer applications immediately; lush vegetative growth accelerates fungal mycelial spread
Foliar feed with soluble potassium silicate (reinforces leaf cuticle thickness against fungal appressorial penetration)
Provide light calcium nitrate feeding once new leaf emergence resumes
irrigation: Terminate all overhead irrigation immediately; convert exclusively to subsurface drip lines
Irrigate strictly between 6:00 AM and 9:00 AM so solar radiation quickly dries any residual humidity
Ensure soil moisture tension is maintained around -20 to -30 kPa to prevent root waterlogging
prevention: Plant scorch-resistant cultivars (e.g., Allstar, Honeoye, or Jewel where available)
Renovate strawberry beds post-harvest by mowing foliage above crowns and raking away all crop residue
Maintain a 3-foot bed width with clean inter-row aisles to promote rapid wind drying
Sanitize pruning shears in 10% household bleach or 70% ethanol between plant rows
recovery_tips: Burn or deeply bury (minimum 12 inches) all pruned infected foliage; do not leave clippings in walkways
Mow and renovate crowns after final harvest, applying a post-harvest protective copper barrier
Monitor newly emerging runner leaves weekly for micro-purple flecks
